problem: Transforming unstructured business document information (such as raw text or scanned documents) into a structured format for downstream systems, specifically focusing on Key-Information Extraction (KIE) and Line Items Recognition (LIR) (p.1).
methodology: Modeling business document information extraction as a tool use problem and presenting Retrieval Augmented Generation (RASG), which combines Retrieval Augmented Generation, Supervised Finetuning, Structured Generation, and Structured Prompting (p.1). The paper also proposes a heuristic algorithm for bounding box backcalculation without vision encoders and a new metric class called General Line Items Recognition Metric (GLIRM) (p.1).
dataset: The DocILE dataset, a large-scale research benchmark for evaluating KIE and LIR from semi-structured business documents like invoices (p.3).
results: GPT-3.5 + RASG achieved 75.40% KIE F1 Score and 79.81% LIR GLIRM-F1, while Hermes 2 Pro + RASG achieved 73.41% KIE F1 Score and 69.44% LIR GLIRM-F1, outperforming or competing with strong multimodal baselines (p.3). The median table-level Information Coverage Score (ICS) for bounding box backcalculation was 87.79% for GPT-3.5 + RASG and 85.02% for Hermes 2 Pro + RASG, compared to 92.93% for the best baseline (p.4).
key_findings: Large Language Models (LLMs) with RASG are competitive with or surpass current state-of-the-art Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) without RASG on business document information extraction benchmarks (p.1). For Key-Information Extraction, prompt engineering provides only marginal gains compared to retrieval or finetuning, whereas for Line Items Recognition, prompt engineering is as important as retrieval and finetuning (p.4).
